newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Prodi says Italy not trying to "offset" Germany.
newsitem.headline: Prodi says Italy not trying to "offset" Germany.

text.p: Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi said on Wednesday his goal was not to offset German influence in Europe but NATO needed to focus increasingly on southern Europe.

"We actually never said we wanted to offset anyone, especially because we cannot be more ambitious than our roles justify," Prodi said in Hungary when asked at a news conference if Italy saw itself as a counterbalance to Germany.
"We want Europe and NATO to establish a balance between north and south Europe because these organisations represent every European country and every European culture," he said.
"We cannot envisage a Europe where the Latin countries and cultures do not take an active part (and) as far as NATO is concerned that is becoming more and more obvious day by day."

"Most important issues concern the southern part of Europe, the south-eastern part actually, therefore it is quite clear that when we are talking about NATO expansion we cannot disregard this," he said.
Prodi spoke at a joint news conference with Hungarian Prime Minister Gyula Horn who said Italy had agreed to help create a fund to boost small- and medium-sized businesses in Hungary.

"It is well known I believe that in Italy the SME sector is most dynamic and...the establishment of a Hungarian-Italian country fund may be an important way forward," Horn said following two days of talks with Prodi.
He did not give any financial details of how the fund would operate but said that developing this sector could help Hungary overcome problems with reducing its budget deficits.

Horn said Hungary and Italy had agreed on several other points, including encouraging Italian investment in Hungary's medical tourism industry and making it easier for Hungarians to be employed as seasonal workers in Italy.
The two countries agreed to have identification cards suffice as travel documents and to open honorary consulates, the prime ministers said.
Horn said Italy fully supported Hungary's bid for integration into NATO and the EU and added: "We established that for Hungary, Italy is a strategic partner."
